messages:
marta: noticed weird rows in org-usage table, looks like other orgs' metrics showing up for my tenant. anyone else? :white_flag:
frances: which query/view? screenshots?
marta: Admin -> Org Usage -> group by org -> top row shows Org 202 with 9k tokens but my X-Org-ID=707. clicking into row shows payload ownerOrg:202.
sam: can you paste the API call?
marta: POST /internal/metrics/aggregate  X-Org-ID:707 body: {group_by:["org"], filters:{org:707}} response cached=true rows:[{org:202,value:9000}]
frances: hmmm. I shipped metrics-agg-v3 earlier with a cache-key change to dedupe by group+window. might have removed org from key to reduce cardinality.
leo: was that behind canary?
frances: yes 20% canary in prod.
bel: immediate plan: 1) drop canary to 0% 2) add runtime guard: if cached row.org != request.org -> bypass and emit metric 3) schedule targeted purge for keys created during window.
sam: prefer guard first then purge. large-scale purge could be heavy.
frances: ok will revert canary now and open PR to include org in cache key: `agg:{org}:{group_hash}:{window}`. adding assertion tests for cached org==request.org.
deploy-bot: deploy request received: rollback metrics-agg-v3 -> executing
deploy-bot: rollback complete ✅
leo: add alert rule: metrics.cache.org_mismatch -> page on first occurrence.
frances: also adding lint to infra-libs to forbid cache templates that lack `{org}` for tenant-scoped endpoints.
bel: CSMs alerted for affected customers, asked if they want scrub.
marta: found two flair keys in staging and one in prod tied to acme-inc, logged incident.
frances: will coordinate postmortem and add runbook step: small canary + 24h observation for any cache-key changes.
sam: noted. capturing action items in ticket ENG-9042.
